title: The Mosby Route
logline: Stuck in limo traffic, Ted bets the gang that his zero-left-turn cab route is the fastest way across Manhattan. A cab, a subway and a limo race to Robin's impossible dinner reservation, everyone cheats, and Ranjit's fastest route exposes why Barney's rides home always take forty minutes.
coldOpen: Kids, every New Yorker is certain they know the fastest way across Manhattan. In the fall of 2011, I put mine to the test against a subway, a limo and my four best friends. I was right about everything, except the part where it was fast.

couch.line: Is this the left turn story?
Absolutely not. Well. A little bit.

guests.name: Sal
guests.role: a thirty-one-year cab veteran who obeys every passenger instruction exactly, with zero expression, and knows Ted's reputation among cabbies

guests.name: Odile
guests.role: Ottavia's maitre d', who runs the reservation book like a border crossing and gives tables away to the second

scenes.summary: Gridlock on 42nd Street, twenty-nine minutes before Robin's table disappears. Ted brags about the Mosby Route, Lily backs the subway, Barney backs Ranjit and his routes named after women he fled. The bet: last one to Ottavia pays. Ted and the Eriksens bail. Barney demands the fastest route; it's named after his mother.

beats.line: Kids, it was seven-thirty, and Barney's limo had moved four feet in ten minutes.
Robin says if we're not all there by eight, we lose the table.
beats.title: Robin

messages.text: Ottavia gives the table away at 8:00 if we're not all here.
Not 8:01. The maitre d' has a stopwatch.
Stuck on 42nd. Barney says traffic parts for limos.

beats.line: We have been behind this bus so long, I know the driver's name. It is Doug.
This is why I take cabs. A limo is just a hotel room stuck in traffic.
Ted. That is the most beautiful thing you've ever said.
In a cab, I'd be on the Mosby Route. Tenth Avenue to Hudson, zero left turns. Eighteen minutes.
Ted has been timing the Mosby Route since 1999. It has never once been eighteen minutes.
Left turns are where New York keeps its traffic.
Subway. Express to Chambers. Fifteen minutes, and nobody has to hear about left turns.
Amateurs. Ranjit knows routes you people can't even dream of. Ranjit?
That depends. Is anyone chasing us tonight?
Not yet.
Then we take the Jessica.
What's the Jessica?
Every route is named after a woman Mr. Barney ran away from. The Jessica avoids all fire stations.
Her husband had a very big ladder.
Okay. Bet. Ottavia only makes twelve meatballs a night. First one there gets one.
And the last one there pays for everybody's dinner.
You're on. See you at Ottavia. In eighteen minutes.
It has never once been eighteen minutes!
Marshall. Move. Go, go, go.
Bye, Ranjit! Say hi to Doug!
Ranjit. Forget the Jessica. Give me the fastest route you've got.
The fastest? But Mr. Barney, you never want the fastest.
Tonight I do. What's it called?
The Loretta. It is named after your mother.
Floor it.

scenes.summary: Marshall wants to win clean. Lily wants to win. Ted's gloating selfie shows his cab's medallion number, and Marshall chooses the meatball over his principles. Ted's 'trust me, buddy' text exposes a lifetime of lies. Marshall adds one more charge to the stolen-cab report.

beats.line: Express to Chambers. Ted's in a cab, and Barney's in a parking lot with a minibar.
And we're going to win clean, Lilypad. Minnesota clean.
Baby, I got twenty-two kindergartners through the Met without anyone licking a painting. I can beat Ted to a meatball.
Ted sent a selfie from his cab. Enjoy your rats.
beats.title: Ted

messages.text: Here's me. In a cab. Winning.

beats.line: And look. His medallion number. Right behind his big dumb head.
Lily. Why do you need his medallion number?
Marshall. Do you want to win clean, or do you want the meatball?
Call the taxi commission.
Hi! I'd like to report a stolen cab. Seven J forty-one. The thief has a big dumb head.
Ted just texted me. The express is flooded at Fourteenth, get off and walk. Trust me, buddy.
Buddy? He's lying. Ted only says buddy when he's lying.
Ted says buddy all the time.
Yes.
He called me buddy in his best man speech.
Give me that phone.
Hi, me again. The thief also refuses to turn left. That's not a crime. I just think you should know.

scenes.summary: Ted micromanages Sal, a thirty-one-year cabbie, around the same block three times. Ted's fantasy of arriving first. Sal knows Ted by reputation. Lily's stolen-cab report and Barney's marching band land. Ted bails out on foot without paying.

beats.line: Meanwhile, the Mosby Route was going exactly as planned.
Right on 34th. Right on Ninth. Then right on 33rd.
So, a left. With extra steps.
Three rights make a left, Sal. It's basic geometry.
It's basic circles.
But you're the boss.
Picture it. I walk into Ottavia first, and everyone finally admits I was right.
Ted, you were right. A limo is just a hotel room stuck in traffic.
Eighteen minutes on the dot. Teach us about left turns.
Slowly.
Well. It all begins with the Manhattan grid plan of 1811.
Ooh. Eighteen eleven.
We've passed this hot dog cart three times.
It's a different hot dog cart.
He's waved every time.
Sal, thirty-one years driving this city, and you've never heard of the Mosby Route?
Sure I have. Guy who gives directions, never turns left, tips eleven percent. Every cabbie knows you.
I tip eleven percent because it's a prime number.
So is twenty-three.
Also, dispatch says this cab was reported stolen. Thief has a big dumb head.
Lily!
And there's a marching band crossing Tenth. Forty guys in suits, marching very, very slowly.
Barney!
How far to Ottavia?
Eleven blocks.
Then the Mosby Route continues on foot. Keep the change!
There's no change. There was never any money.

scenes.summary: Robin defends her table for five against Odile's stopwatch. Barney arrives first via the Loretta. The Eriksens lose the meatball. With seconds left, Sal walks in with Ted's phone and Robin seats him as Ted. Ted arrives last, beaten by his own cab, which turned left. Ranjit explains why Barney's rides home take forty minutes.

beats.line: Meanwhile, at Ottavia, Aunt Robin had been holding a table for five since seven-fifteen.
Madame. It is seven forty-four. Your table for five has one person at it.
The other four are racing across Manhattan to see me.
Of course they are.
I gave Sandy Rivers my New Year's countdown for this table. Nobody is taking it.
At eight, it goes to a man who owns a hockey team.
Which team?
Daddy's home! Nine minutes from 42nd Street!
Nine minutes? How?
Ranjit took the Loretta. Apparently I run from my mother faster than anyone.
Second place! Somebody point me to a meatball!
The gentleman in the suit ordered the last one.
I don't even like meatballs. I just like you not having one.
We committed a crime for that meatball.
Misdemeanor. I looked it up on the train.
Seven fifty-nine. Your party is incomplete.
Anybody here know a Ted Mosby? He left his phone in my cab. And his fare.
Ted! You made it! Sit down, Ted.
You're the boss.
Party of five. Complete.
Eleven blocks on foot, Barney. Through your marching band.
They're on retainer. I've been waiting six years to use them.
Did I win?
Ted. You lost to your own cab.
Sal? How did you beat me here?
I turned left.
And you are?
Ted Mosby, archi—
He's nobody. He's paying.
Hello! I found parking. It is in New Jersey.
Ranjit. Nine minutes tonight. So why does the ride home from the bar take forty?
After the bar, you are sad. So I take the long way, past all the lights, until you are happy.
I call it the Barney. It is the only route where you are not running from anybody.
Ranjit. That's the nicest thing anyone has ever—
Also, I charge by the hour.
Kids, Ranjit eventually named a route after me, too. It's how he escapes my lectures on left turns. It's his fastest.
